title: Prober-driven schema gate with probabilistic function-call diff thresholds and staged unwind
creator: Sana Iqbal
description:
Goal: Add a lightweight probing layer that runs parallel (shadow/prober) requests during canaries and A/B slices to detect structured-output and function-call incompatibilities earlier, and automatically trigger a staged unwind when mismatch rates exceed probabilistic thresholds.

Success criteria:
- Detect schema or function-call argument divergence with >90% precision and <2% false positive rate in production-like traffic within first 10k probe events.
- Auto-unwind (canary -> rollback) initiates within configured hysteresis window when the 1-minute rolling mismatch probability exceeds threshold.
- No measurable end-user latency increase for primary traffic (probe traffic is shadowed).

Design overview:
1) Prober agents: small, deterministic probe variants that exercise edge-shaped prompts and typical tool-calling surfaces. Probers run as shadow requests (non-blocking) at a configurable sample rate per route (default 2%).
2) Differential comparator: lightweight sawtooth comparator that computes three signals per invocation: schema-structure-diff (shape/type mismatch), named-arg-diff (missing/extra keys), and semantics-fail (function invoked unexpectedly). Each signal is boolean per probe.
3) Probabilistic gate: instead of hard counts, we maintain exponentially-weighted mismatch probability per route and model-variant; the gate trips when P(mismatch) > configured threshold (default 0.015) sustained for N windows (default 3).
4) Staged unwind actions: on trip, first reduce rollout percentage by 50% and notify canary watchers; if sustained, fully revert to last stable variant and execute incident runbook.

Telemetry & monitoring:
- Metrics: probe.invocations, probe.mismatch.{schema,args,semantics}, probe.mismatch_probability, probe.rollback_trigger_count, probe.latency_p95_shadow.
- Dashboards: canary-compatibility (per-route, per-variant) with a drilldown to failed probes (payload hashes + example diffs).
- Alerts: Pager alert when rollback_trigger_count > 0 for a paid customer route and severity is high. Slack notification to #rollouts for non-prod.

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Probabilistic thresholding reduces noisy rollbacks from low-count random divergences but requires careful tuning to avoid delayed detection for high-latency bugs. We prefer EWMA-based probability over fixed counts to adapt across traffic profiles.
- Shadow probes avoid user-facing latency but increase egress and runtime cost; we scope probes to 2% by default and allow burst budgets.
- Comparator must be conservative on schema (type/shape) but aggressive on required named args for tool-calling safety.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for comparator logic + fuzz harness that generates pairwise function-call variants.
- Integration: run prober against model-variants in staging with a replay of production prompt corpus (dataset: canary-prober-replay-2026-02).
- Canary: enable shadow probes at 2% for first 24h then evaluate mismatch_probability; ramp to 5% for second 24h.

Rollout strategy:
- Feature flag gated (canary-compat-prober) plus per-customer opt-out.
- Initial alpha on internal routes and selected non-prod customers.
- Ramp plan: internal -> sandbox customers -> small set of production routes (low-risk) -> global.

Runbook excerpt (automated portion):
1) Gate trips => reduce rollout_pct *= 0.5, send automated Slack message and create a temporary incident channel.
2) If sustained for 3 windows => revert variant, annotate rollout with reason and attach failing probe sample.
3) Post-mortem triggers if rollback happened on >1 route within 24 hours.

Open implementation notes & blockers:
- Need a compact canonical diff format to store probe failures in telemetry without PII; blocked by privacy review (SEC-PRIV-41).
- Runtime integration: lightweight comparator must run in serving path's shadow pipeline; avoid allocating large objects to not perturb GC in host process.
- Edge case: cached responses (KV cache) can mask mismatches for some probes; we're adding a probe header to force no-cache for probe traffic.

Artifacts & references:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/PROBER-GATE-2026
- GitHub sketch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1782 (prober scaffolding)
- Telemetry dashboard (Datadog): https://app.datadog.com/dashboard/canary-compat-2026
- Probe corpus (internal GCS): gs://redwood-canary/probes/2026-02-replay.jsonl

Next steps (this sprint):
- Complete comparator C implementation and land PR for shadow pipeline integration.
- Finalize canonical diff schema with security & product.
- Add alerting rules and dashboard panels for first-run alpha.

Acceptance criteria for this ticket:
- Shadow probe pipeline lives in runtime and can be toggled by per-route config.
- Comparator produces telemetry metrics and example diff payloads (sanitized).
- Automated staged unwind executes on simulated trip in integration tests.
